name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q01 - Types of movement and their examples

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II and select the correct option.

List I (Type of Movement)List II (Example / Function)
(A) Amoeboid movement(i) Removal of dust particles in trachea
(B) Ciliary movement(ii) Movement of jaws and tongue
(C) Flagellar movement(iii) Macrophages and leucocytes
(D) Muscular movement(iv) Swimming of spermatozoa

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cells and organs of the human body exhibit distinct types of movements—amoeboid, ciliary, flagellar, and muscular—each mediated by specialised cellular or tissue structures.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Amoeboid movement is effected by pseudopodia formed by protoplasmic streaming and microfilaments, and is exhibited by macrophages and leucocytes in blood.
- Ciliary movement occurs in internal tubular organs lined by ciliated epithelium, such as the trachea, where coordinated ciliary beating removes inhaled dust particles.
- Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa (as well as maintaining water current in sponges and locomotion in Euglena).
- Muscular movement uses the contractile property of muscles for moving limbs, jaws, and the tongue.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is Amoeboid movement with Macrophages and leucocytes, Ciliary movement with Removal of dust particles in trachea, Flagellar movement with Swimming of spermatozoa, and Muscular movement with Movement of jaws and tongue, corresponding to (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II and choose the correct combination.

List I (Structure / Muscle Type)List II (Characteristic)
(A) Skeletal muscle(i) Branched, striated, and involuntary
(B) Visceral muscle(ii) Striated and voluntary
(C) Cardiac muscle(iii) Muscle bundle held by fascia
(D) Fascicle(iv) Non-striated and involuntary

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Muscles are classified based on location, microscopic appearance (striations), and regulation (voluntary or involuntary), while organised skeletal muscles consist of bundles of fibres.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Skeletal muscles are closely associated with skeletal components, appear striped (striated) under the microscope, and are under voluntary control of the nervous system.
- Visceral muscles line hollow visceral organs, lack striations (smooth/non-striated), and are involuntary.
- Cardiac muscles are the muscles of the heart; their cells assemble in a branching pattern, appear striated, and are involuntary.
- Fascicles are muscle bundles held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct pairing is (A)-(ii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding the ultrastructure of a myofibril.

List I (Region / Line)List II (Description)
(A) Z line(i) Thin fibrous membrane holding thick filaments
(B) M line(ii) Functional unit of contraction
(C) H zone(iii) Elastic fibre bisecting the I band
(D) Sarcomere(iv) Central part of thick filament not overlapped by thin filaments

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each myofibril has alternate dark (A) and light (I) bands due to the arrangement of actin (thin) and myosin (thick) filaments, organised into repeating contractile units.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- The Z line is an elastic fibre in the centre of each I band that bisects it and anchors the thin filaments.
- The M line is a thin fibrous membrane in the middle of the A band that holds the thick filaments together.
- The H zone is the central part of the thick filament that is not overlapped by thin filaments in the resting state.
- The sarcomere is the portion of the myofibril between two successive Z lines and serves as the functional unit of contraction.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q04 - Contractile proteins and their specific roles

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Contractile Protein / Component) with List II (Structure / Function) and select the correct option.

List IList II
(A) F-actin(i) Monomeric protein constituting thick filament
(B) Troponin(ii) Polymer of monomeric G-actins
(C) Meromyosin(iii) Active ATPase enzyme with ATP and actin binding sites
(D) Globular head of HMM(iv) Masks active sites for myosin on actin in resting state

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Thin and thick myofilaments are composed of specialised polymerised contractile and regulatory proteins.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Each actin (thin) filament has two helically wound F (filamentous) actins, where each F-actin is a polymer of monomeric G (globular) actins.
- Troponin is a complex protein distributed at regular intervals on tropomyosin; in the resting state, a subunit of troponin masks the active binding sites for myosin on the actin filaments.
- Meromyosins are the monomeric proteins that polymerise to constitute one thick (myosin) filament.
- The globular head of heavy meromyosin (HMM) functions as an active ATPase enzyme and possesses binding sites for ATP as well as active sites for actin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(ii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q05 - Muscle contraction physiology and fibre types

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding muscle physiology and fibre types.

List IList II
(A) Red muscle fibres(i) High sarcoplasmic reticulum and anaerobic energy
(B) White muscle fibres(ii) Accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic glycogen breakdown
(C) Acetylcholine(iii) High myoglobin content and plenty of mitochondria
(D) Muscle fatigue(iv) Neurotransmitter generating action potential in sarcolemma

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Muscle excitation involves neuromuscular transmission, while sustained contraction depends on aerobic or anaerobic metabolism in red and white muscle fibres.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Red muscle fibres (aerobic muscles) have high myoglobin content and plenty of mitochondria to utilise stored oxygen for ATP production.
- White muscle fibres have very little myoglobin and few mitochondria, possess a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum, and depend on anaerobic processes for energy.
- Acetylcholine is the neurotransmitter released at the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate) that generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.
- Muscle fatigue results from repeated activation of muscles, leading to the accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic breakdown of glycogen.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct pairing is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q06 - Bone counts in human axial skeleton

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Axial Skeleton Component) with List II (Number of Bones) in an adult human.

List IList II
(A) Cranial bones(i) 14
(B) Facial skeletal elements(ii) 12
(C) Cervical vertebrae(iii) 8
(D) Thoracic vertebrae(iv) 7

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The axial skeleton comprises 80 bones distributed along the main axis of the body, including the skull and the vertebral column.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Cranial bones are 8 in number and form the hard protective outer covering (cranium) for the brain.
- The facial region is made up of 14 skeletal elements forming the front part of the skull.
- The cervical region of the vertebral column consists of 7 vertebrae in almost all mammals including human beings.
- The thoracic region of the vertebral column consists of 12 vertebrae.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q07 - Pectoral and pelvic girdle anatomical features

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Girdle Structure) with List II (Anatomical Feature) and select the correct option.

List IList II
(A) Scapula(i) Cavity formed by fusion of ilium, ischium, and pubis
(B) Glenoid cavity(ii) Large triangular flat bone between 2nd and 7th ribs
(C) Acetabulum(iii) Ventral meeting of pelvic girdle halves with fibrous cartilage
(D) Pubic symphysis(iv) Depression below acromion articulating with head of humerus

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The pectoral and pelvic girdles articulate the forelimbs and hindlimbs, respectively, with the axial skeleton.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- The scapula is a large triangular flat bone situated in the dorsal part of the thorax between the second and seventh ribs.
- The glenoid cavity is a depression below the acromion of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint.
- The acetabulum is a cavity at the point of fusion of the ilium, ischium, and pubis of each coxal bone, to which the thigh bone (femur) articulates.
- The pubic symphysis is formed where the two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally, containing fibrous cartilage.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct pairing is (A)-(ii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_LOCOMOTIONANDMOVEMENT_MCQ_Q08 - Synovial joints and their anatomical locations

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Type of Synovial Joint) with List II (Example / Location) and choose the correct option.

List IList II
(A) Ball and socket joint(i) Knee joint
(B) Hinge joint(ii) Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb
(C) Pivot joint(iii) Between humerus and pectoral girdle
(D) Saddle joint(iv) Between atlas and axis

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synovial joints contain a fluid-filled synovial cavity between articulating surfaces, permitting considerable movement of various types.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- The ball and socket joint is present between the humerus and the pectoral girdle (glenoid cavity).
- The hinge joint is exemplified by the knee joint.
- The pivot joint is found between the atlas and the axis vertebrae.
- The saddle joint occurs between the carpal and the metacarpal of the thumb.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(i), (C)-(iv), (D)-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match List I (Disorder) with List II (Cause / Characteristic) and select the correct combination.

List IList II
(A) Myasthenia gravis(i) Decreased bone mass due to decreased estrogen levels
(B) Tetany(ii) Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction
(C) Osteoporosis(iii) Joint inflammation due to uric acid crystals
(D) Gout(iv) Rapid muscle spasms due to low \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) in body fluid

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Disorders of the muscular and skeletal systems arise from autoimmune, ionic, hormonal, or metabolic abnormalities.

Step 2: Matching Each Item
- Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction, leading to fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscle.
- Tetany is characterised by rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle due to low \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) levels in body fluid.
- Osteoporosis is an age-related disorder characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chances of fractures, commonly caused by decreased levels of estrogen.
- Gout is the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation of uric acid crystals.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(ii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(iii).
